editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a bleak, old hospital in Russia where the walls feel like they are closing in on you. You follow a doctor who thinks he is above everyone else, but he finds himself fascinated by a former student who has been locked away in Ward 6. The student is smart, loud, and doesn't care about the rules, which makes the doctor question his own quiet, boring life. It is a slow burn that feels more like a stage play than a typical movie, focusing on the weird power struggle between the man in charge and the man in chains.

What really hits home is how the doctor starts to lean on the patient for mental support, only to have his other coworkers laugh at him for it. The acting is top-notch and makes the depressing setting feel real. It is not a fast movie, so you need some patience, but the payoff is worth it.
endingExplained: The story takes a dark turn when the doctor realizes he is not as safe as he thinks. After trying to help his student, the doctor is eventually locked up in the same ward himself. He ends up as a patient in the very place he used to run. He learns the hard way that the system he served is cruel to everyone, and there is no easy way out of the madness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep stories about human nature and old world settings.
similarMovies: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
